results.title: CMS Policy Article A52467 - PAP devices, coding guidelines (companion to LCD L33718)
results.text:
# CPAP/PAP device coding guidelines and diagnosis requirements

## Overview

Positive airway pressure devices fall under the Durable Medical Equipment benefit category. For Medicare payment the equipment must meet the reasonable and necessary standard in the related Local Coverage Determination (L33718) and the specific statutory payment requirements.

## Diagnosis code requirements

The only diagnosis code that supports medical necessity for PAP therapy is G47.33 (obstructive sleep apnea). Having the code does not by itself guarantee coverage: the supplier must verify that all applicable coverage criteria in the LCD are met. ICD-10 codes other than G47.33 are treated as not supporting medical necessity for PAP devices, so other diagnoses cannot justify PAP claims.

results.text:
# Coverage indications for PAP devices in obstructive sleep apnea

## Initial Medicare coverage requirements

Three foundational criteria must be met. The item must fall within a defined Medicare benefit category. It must be reasonable and necessary for diagnosing or treating illness or injury or improving the function of a malformed body member. All other applicable statutory and regulatory requirements must be met.

The policy distinguishes E0601 (single-level continuous positive airway pressure, CPAP) from E0470 (bi-level respiratory assist device without backup rate). Both treat obstructive sleep apnea when specific conditions are documented.

final_text:
**Most plausible reason code: CARC 11.** The project's reference paraphrases it as "The diagnosis doesn't support the procedure billed." It maps to the project rule `dx_procedure_mismatch`. Here the claim's HCPCS code is A7035, which the tool describes as headgear used with a positive airway pressure device. The principal diagnosis is Z733, which the tool describes as "Stress, not elsewhere classified".

CMS Policy Article A52467 (PAP devices coding guidelines) says G47.33 is the only diagnosis code that supports medical necessity for PAP therapy. It says other ICD-10 codes are treated as not supporting it. The text I retrieved doesn't say whether this covers headgear accessories such as A7035, so that link is an inference. I didn't check prior authorization (CARC 197), so I can't rule it out.

**How the score relates:** the model gives a denial probability of 0.2426. The validation average is 0.1805, so the claim is 1.34 times the average, or 6.2 percentage points higher. The model doesn't predict reason codes, so the score doesn't confirm CARC 11.

- The model weighs HCPCS A7035 upward (+0.29 log-odds, +34% odds).
- The model weighs place of service 22 (on-campus outpatient hospital) upward (+0.287, +33% odds). This feature isn't in the data dictionary.
- The model weighs Z733 slightly downward (−0.118, −11% odds). That is the opposite of what a diagnosis mismatch would suggest.

These are things the model weighs, not causes of denial. The denial label in this project is synthetic, so any CARC here is illustrative and not a real payer decision.
